item.text: {"0":"Across all four datasets, set causal recency-pooling readout_mix=0.40 and readout_half_life=4 interactions. This improved validation on the preceding input program; test whether broader recent-interest retention also helps the current popularity-change-scaled inputs. Mask padding and use identical causal pooling during training and inference, selecting the final real position. Preserve all other components and update predictor metadata consistently.","1":"Across all four datasets, increase only the pointwise logistic coefficient from 0.2 to 0.4: softplus(negative-positive)+0.4*[softplus(-positive)+softplus(negative)], with the existing nonpadding reduction. This improved the preceding input program; stronger absolute-score supervision may also stabilize the current popularity-change-scaled model. Preserve sampling, embeddings, GRU topology, readout, scoring and optimizer.","2":"Across all four datasets, jointly set learning rate=0.001 and dropout=0.20, retaining maxlen=128, width=128 and one GRU layer. Larger updates may learn sparse item representations faster, while moderately stronger dropout limits overfitting from those updates. Unlike the previously regressed shorter-history/lower-rate configuration, retain the existing history coverage. Preserve loss, embedding design, readout, batch size, seed 42, 200 batches per epoch and the 200-epoch cap.","3":"Across all four datasets, tie the output embedding weight to the input embedding weight while retaining unit normalization, width=128 and zero padding. Shared item representations may improve statistical efficiency for sparse items and remove disagreement between independently trained input and candidate vectors. Preserve the GRU, popularity-change input scaling, history policy, readout, dot-product scoring, loss and optimizer. Update model construction and predictor loading so each category restores one consistently tied checkpoint."}
